source.title: Intraclass clustering: an implicit learning ability that regularizes DNNs

record.tranche_reason: The study measures magnitude-aware sharpness and compares its association with generalization across hyperparameter variations, using the granulated Kendall coefficient. It does not reproduce the original study’s broader comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for its own intraclass-clustering measures as well as sharpness measures. Rows below retain sharpness results relevant to V7; the intraclass-clustering results are summarized in fits_no_version because no claim version specifically names those measures. Cited results from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study computes Jiang et al.'s magnitude-aware sharpness measures and granulated Kendall correlations on its own trained networks. Most networks reach approximately 100% training accuracy, making held-out performance informative about generalization gaps. It extends the evaluation to additional architectures, datasets and training conditions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record correctly summarizes the measure comparison but understates the main conclusion: the authors interpret their results as evidence that intraclass clustering emerges during standard supervised training and may provide implicit regularization. Their evidence is correlational, and the mechanisms remain unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the granulated Kendall correlation protocol and magnitude-aware sharpness measures associated with Jiang et al. (2020), across more than 500 models and several dataset-architecture pairs; the study's main proposed measures are intraclass-clustering measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The sharpness measures' Kendall coefficients vary by dataset-architecture pair and hyperparameter variation; worst-case variants perform particularly well when batch size varies.

fits_no_version.finding: Intraclass-clustering measures have higher overall predictive scores than the tested sharpness measures in all three settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Intraclass-clustering measures predict held-out performance across training hyperparameters.

fits_no_version.finding: Intraclass-clustering measures generally increase with depth, and differences between high- and low-performing networks emerge mainly early in training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Intraclass structure emerges during supervised training and differs with generalization performance.

fits_no_version.finding: VGG configurations with dropout 0.4 were excluded because they could not reach approximately 100% training accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: High dropout can impair fitting in the tested VGG training recipe.

record.problems: The evidence is correlational, and the authors say mechanisms remain undisclosed. The tables provide Kendall coefficients but no uncertainty estimates. Several hyperparameter covariations were deliberately excluded; the VGG configurations with dropout rate 0.4 were also omitted because those networks could not reach approximately 100% training accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: Intraclass-clustering measure results, including their coefficients across hyperparameters and layer/training-trajectory plots, are described under fits_no_version rather than given row-by-row because no listed version names those measures. No reported sharpness result was omitted from the extracted tables.

untested.parts: No natural-label versus random-label training and held-out comparison.
No test-error trajectory across the interpolation threshold in the specified fully connected networks.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
Optimizer choices vary, but the supplied results do not report the direction or size of Adam versus SGD held-out performance differences.
Batch sizes vary under a common training schedule, but sharpness correlations do not establish whether larger batches worsen held-out performance.
No reported held-out dropout benefit or penalty. Excluding VGG configurations with dropout 0.4 for poor training fit does not measure their test-error effect.

No comparison with norm- or margin-based measures, no SVHN evaluation, and no causal test. Results generally use held-out performance with approximately saturated training accuracy rather than explicitly reporting gap correlations; augmentation conditions are pooled in several scores.
No removal and retraining experiment based on example memorization.

missing.what: Unrecorded conditional sharpness coefficients materially qualify the overall scores. For CIFAR100 superclasses, random sharpness under augmentation is -0.58; alternate random sharpness under dropout is -0.05; worst-case sharpness under width/depth is -0.03/-0.09; alternate worst-case sharpness under augmentation is -0.08. Record all omitted hyperparameter columns, including the strong learning-rate associations.

CIFAR100 conditional results are omitted: batch-size coefficients are 0.68, 0.61, 0.96 and 0.91; random sharpness under augmentation is -0.62; alternate random sharpness under dropout is -0.06; worst-case sharpness under width/depth is -0.16/-0.23; alternate worst-case sharpness under augmentation is -0.25. Other omitted columns are needed to show implementation sensitivity.

CIFAR10 conditional results are omitted: standard random sharpness gives -0.25 for weight decay, -0.04 for dropout and -0.27 for augmentation; its alternate version gives 0.92 for dropout. Worst-case sharpness gives 0.15 for width and 0.06 for depth; alternate worst-case sharpness gives -0.15 for depth. Batch-size coefficients are 0.62, 0.67, 0.89 and 0.67.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V7. Positive average correlations do not imply reliable tracking under every hyperparameter. Negative conditional coefficients qualify extensions across these settings, but pooled augmentation conditions prevent treating them as clean refutations of V7's original no-augmentation setting. The record's assertion that no sharpness results were omitted is incorrect.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not compare magnitude-aware sharpness with the norm- and margin-based measures named in the version. Its reported values are correlations across hyperparameter variations, not a direct perturbation-tolerance comparison among networks selected for similarly low training loss.
